title: Load-adaptive microbatch allocator with KV-compaction hysteresis
creator: Aisha Gupta
description: Under sustained high QPS, our continuous batching pipeline occasionally creates long-lived microbatches that cause KV cache pressure and GPU OOM risk for mixed-size requests. This ticket designs and implements a load-adaptive microbatch allocator that proactively signals KV-compaction hysteresis and incremental backpressure to protect tail latency and prevent OOMs while preserving throughput for common fast paths.
background: Recent incidents (see ENG-61207) show that when a small fraction of long-context/large-token requests arrive during sustained peak load, microbatch growth combined with KV retention leads to GPU memory fragmentation and slow compaction cycles. Existing admission controllers are threshold-based and oscillate under bursty traffic, causing repeated cache evictions that harm subsequent generations. We need a smoother, history-aware approach that ties microbatch admission thresholds to a predictive GPU headroom estimator and a KV-compaction hysteresis window.
goals: Introduce a load-adaptive microbatch admission allocator that adjusts target microbatch size per model and slot based on measured headroom and request-size distribution
Implement KV-compaction hysteresis to avoid oscillatory evictions (compact only after sustained pressure) and expose a metric for compaction cooldown state
Add graded backpressure signals (0..3) to upstream request router to allow graceful degradation instead of hard drops
Maintain or improve p50/p95 latency under 95th percentile QPS and reduce OOMs to zero in simulated workloads
Ship with telemetry and canary rollout flags in runtime-1.22
non_goals: Full rewrite of KV cache format
Changing model scheduling across GPUs (this ticket only touches admission logic and compaction heuristics)
acceptance_criteria: Tiered backpressure levels implemented and respected by request router in canary region
KV-compaction enters cooldown state and avoids repeated compactions for identical pressure signals (verified in unit tests and integration stress tests),
End-to-end load tests: under synthetic high-QPS mixed-size workload (90% short gen, 10% long gen) p95 latency no worse than current baseline + 10% while throughput drop < 5%
No GPU OOMs or NV-memory allocation failures during 24h soak in canary clusters
Dashboard widgets: compaction_hysteresis_state, headroom_estimate, microbatch_target_size, backpressure_level (per-model) added to console observability
implementation_plan: Design: introduce HeadroomEstimator component (exposes ms-average of resident GPU allocs, predicted allocation curve over next 1s)
Design: microbatch allocator uses a weighted moving-average of recent request token sizes + HeadroomEstimator to compute target microbatch token cap per slot
Design: KV-compaction hysteresis: require consecutive pressure windows (configurable, default 3s) before full compaction and add exponential cooldown (min 5s, max 60s)
Proto: implement HeadroomEstimator shim and unit tests (ENG branch: feat/microbatch/headroom-estimator)
Proto: add allocator hooks into admission service; expose microbatch_target_size metric
Integration: wire graded backpressure levels (0=none,1=soft-defer,2=prefer-compact-variant,3=reject) to request-router with RBAC flag for canary
Test: create synthetic load generator scenarios (small vs large token mixes) and run in CI-long with simulated GPU memory pressure
Canary: rollout to 2 racks in us-west-2; monitor dashboards and run 24h soak
Rollout: expand to global canaries and then default enable after 2 weeks with rollback playbook
risks: Estimator drift: HeadroomEstimator may underpredict allocations for pathological request mixes => risk of OOM if calibrations are wrong
Latency regressions for long-tail requests if backpressure levels are too aggressive
Interference with model-priority lanes and autoscaler assumptions; need to coordinate with Dedicated autoscaling team
Dashboards may not capture per-slot granularity initially, making debugging slower
test_plan: Unit tests for HeadroomEstimator (edge cases: sudden spike, slow ramp, noisy samples)
Property tests for hysteresis (ensure compaction cooldown enforced)
Integration stress tests: mixed workload generator (90/10 short/long) for 4h with metrics collected
Chaos test: randomly delay compaction worker to emulate slow KV compaction and verify backpressure level changes
Canary soak (24h) with monitoring alerts for OOM, p95 latency, and compaction frequency
observability_and_alerting: Alert if gpu_headroom_estimate < 10% for > 10s in canary clusters
Alert on any OOMs where compaction_hysteresis_state==cooldown
Dashboard panels for per-model backpressure heatmap and compaction frequency
Tracing: annotate traces with backpressure_level and microbatch_target_tokens
rollout_strategy: Canary: enable for low-traffic accounts and 2 racks in us-west-2
Observability guardrails: automatic rollback if OOMs > 0 or p95 latency increases by > 20%
Gradual ramp: 5% -> 25% -> 75% -> 100% over two weeks if metrics stable
notes: Spike test results (2026-03-05): prototype reduced compaction frequency by ~40% and eliminated a class of transient OOMs in synthetic run (see linked PR)
Design review (2026-03-02): PM and infra approved hysteresis but asked for explicit cooldown metric; added compaction_hysteresis_state
Related work: coordinate with Dedicated autoscaler leads (Sofia Ribeiro) to document expected headroom signals
